profile.summary: CodonBERT is a language model for the coding regions of mRNA, built by Sanofi for mRNA vaccine and therapeutic design. It reads a coding sequence codon by codon and outputs an embedding for each codon. These embeddings can be fine-tuned to predict properties such as protein expression and mRNA degradation, to help choose among the many mRNA sequences that encode the same protein.

summary_quotes.text: To enable the selection of an optimal sequence, we developed CodonBERT, a large language model (LLM) for mRNAs.
Even small proteins or peptides can be encoded by an enormously large number of mRNAs.
CodonBERT takes the coding region as input, using codons as tokens, and outputs an embedding that provides contextual codon representations.
including the prediction of protein expression and mRNA degradation

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: CodonBERT is a BERT model of 12 bidirectional transformer encoder layers, each with 12 attention heads and hidden size 768. Each codon is one token: five symbols (A, U, G, C, N) in three positions give 125 codons, plus five special tokens, for a vocabulary of 130. The input is a pair of sequences joined by a separator, embedded with codon, position and segment embeddings. Pretraining combined two tasks: masked language modelling over codons, and sequence taxonomy prediction, in which the model predicts whether the two sequences come from the same one of 14 taxonomic categories. For downstream tasks, the embeddings feed additional trainable layers.

quotes.text: Each transformer layer processes its input using 12 self-attention heads and then outputs a representation for each position with hidden size 768.
Thus, in total, there are 130 tokens in the vocabulary of CodonBERT.
CodonBERT takes a sequence pair as input and concatenates them using a separator token ([SEP]).
CodonBERT constructs the input embedding by concatenating codon, position, and segment embeddings.
We pretrained CodonBERT with two tasks: masked language model (MLM) learning and sequence taxonomy prediction (STP).
50% of the sequence pairs consisted of two sequences belonging to one of the 14 categories.
The embeddings provided by CodonBERT can be combined with additional trainable layers to perform various downstream regression and prediction tasks

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One pretrained PyTorch model is released, as a single zip file (CodonBERT.zip, 954,923,856 bytes, last modified 8 May 2024) on a Sanofi download server rather than a versioned model hub, so the file has no revision identifier beyond its date. The repository holds pretraining and fine-tuning scripts, the NCBI IDs of all 10 million pretraining sequences, a held-out evaluation set, and the downstream datasets including an internal Sanofi set (MLOS.csv). A result should name the repository commit (451a1b16 read here) and the zip file's date or checksum.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: BERT-style masked language model of mRNA coding sequences at codon resolution, with an extra sequence taxonomy prediction task.

quotes.text: we developed CodonBERT, an LLM that extends the BERT model and applies it to the language of mRNAs
masked language model (MLM) learning and sequence taxonomy prediction (STP)

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: 12 bidirectional transformer encoder layers, 12 attention heads, hidden size 768, absolute position embeddings; loaded in code as a Transformers BertForPreTraining model. The repository config sets intermediate size 3072.

quotes.text: a sequence length of 1024, as well as 12 layers, each with 12 attention heads. The model's hidden size is set at 768.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: mRNA coding sequences tokenised into codons (vocabulary of 130 tokens from A, U, G, C, N plus special tokens); one sequence or a pair. The embedding script reads sequences from a FASTA file.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: A contextual embedding for each codon; extract_embed.py saves the last hidden layer per sequence, without the start and end special tokens, to a pickle file. Fine-tuned heads output task predictions such as protein expression or mRNA degradation.

quotes.text: outputs an embedding that provides contextual codon representations

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: About 110 million, as stated in the paper. The sources read give no exact count from the released file.

quotes.text: Overall, the model encompasses about 110 million parameters.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: About 10 million mRNA coding sequences from NCBI: mammalian reference sequences, E. coli reference sequences, human virus complete nucleotides, and yeast strains, labelled into 14 taxonomic categories. Sequences had to be a multiple of three long, start with AUG and end with a stop codon. 1% per category was held out. The NCBI IDs are listed in the repository.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: Combined input of up to 1024 tokens; in pretraining each sequence of a pair was limited to 512 codons, and longer sequences were split into fragments of at most 512. The embedding config sets max_length 1024.

quotes.text: Because the inputs of CodonBERT are sequence pairs, the length of each sequence is limited up to 512 codons; therefore, the length of the combined sequence is less than 1024.
Sequences exceeding the length limitation are split into fragments no longer than 512.

limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The guide stops at installation because the README only links the weights and names the embedding script; it gives no download command and no example invocation.
The extract_embed.py script reads its settings from config.yaml, whose embed paths are empty strings in the repository and must be filled in by the user.

notes: Several unrelated models share the name CodonBERT (for example FPPGroup/CodonBERT, a codon optimisation model, and re-uploads on Hugging Face). This page describes the Sanofi model from Li et al. (Genome Research 2024), which matches the Evo 2 SI reference to Li et al. The licences are custom academic and non-commercial notices, so store_bytes is false for the repository files; the paper is CC BY-NC 4.0, so it is not stored either. artifacts/weights-headers.txt is the response to a HEAD request and will not reproduce byte for byte on a re-fetch.
